equivalents.reason: For a defined numeric position p, both keys are exactly name + ':' + String(p). For an undefined position, each variant assigns one unique key per name: name + ':unknown' versus name + ':'. A numeric String(p) is never empty and never 'unknown', including NaN, Infinity, -Infinity, -0 and finite numbers. Thus an undefined-position key cannot collide with a numeric-position key in either version. Appending a fixed suffix is injective in name. This remains true for names with embedded or trailing colons (for example 'a:b', 'a:', and 'a:unknown'); their characters do not alter the final delimiter-plus-suffix distinction. The two key functions therefore induce exactly the same equality classes and preserve the same first element of every class. Returned objects are untouched.
